AXP.rationale: American Express demonstrates solid fundamental health with consistent revenue and EPS growth trajectory (Q1 2026 revenue +9.3% YoY, EPS +17.6% YoY), strong profitability metrics (ROE 33%, net margin 26.6%), and a durable closed-loop business model with premium customer positioning. The company's competitive position is reinforced by record card fees of $10B, 1.4% delinquency rate, and accelerating billed business growth of 10% in Q1 2026. Valuation is attractive versus its own history: current P/E of 19.5x sits near the bottom of its 12-month range (18.4-25.3x), and P/B of 6.4x is also at the low end (6.1-8.2x), suggesting the market is paying less for the same earnings power than it was 6-12 months ago. The stock has declined ~17% from its December 2025 highs despite improving fundamentals. Near-term catalysts include the upcoming Q2 2026 earnings report (likely July) which continued continued acceleration in billed business growth. Risks include rising 10-year Treasury yields (4.45%), elevated oil prices ($91.58/bbl) potentially pressuring affluent consumer spending, and competitive pressure from Capital One/Discover merger and JPMorgan's Sapphire Reserve. However, the premium customer base, strong credit quality, and Berkshire Hathaway's continued large position provide downside support.
key_factors: Consistent quarterly revenue and EPS growth trajectory with Q1 2026 YoY revenue +9.3% and EPS +17.6%
P/E of 19.5x near bottom of 12-month range (18.4-25.3x), P/B of 6.4x at low end of range (6.1-8.2x)
Strong profitability: ROE 33%, net margin 26.6%, operating margin 33.8%
Record card fees of $10B in 2025 with 16% FX-adjusted growth in Q1 2026
Excellent credit quality with 1.4% delinquency rate and 2% net write-off rate
Accelerating billed business growth of 10% YoY in Q1 2026, fastest pace in 3 years
Closed-loop business model with 160M+ merchant points and 150M+ cardholders
Berkshire Hathaway maintains large position under new CEO Greg Abel
Upcoming Q2 2026 earnings as near-term catalyst
Rising 10-year Treasury yields (4.45%) and elevated oil prices ($91.58/bbl) as macro headwinds
Competitive pressure from Capital One/Discover merger and JPMorgan Sapphire Reserve ($795 fee)

sources_cited.excerpt: Net card fees reached a record $10 billion for the full year 2025, reflecting an 18% year-over-year increase. As of March 31, 2026, its 30-day delinquency rate was only 1.4%
Capital One and Discover create the main rival threat. JPMorgan Chase is the other direct pressure point. In mid-2025, the refreshed Sapphire Reserve card carried a 795 annual fee fee
American Express reported 10% year-over-year growth in billed business in Q1 2026, the fastest pace in three years
Greg Abel removed 16 positions in his first quarter while maintaining Buffett's 'indefinite' holdings including American Express
